value.rationale: The norm of the spectral Riesz projection is a mathematically natural nonnormal eigenvalue-conditioning invariant, not a re-labeled spectral-set computation. The same isolated spectral point exhibits two qualitatively different instability laws when it collides with two distinct branches of the essential spectral curve, with exact sharp logarithmic and inverse-quadratic coefficients. This provides a quantitative benchmark beyond low-degree Weyl and disconnected-spectrum results.
